## Purpose

Tissue of origin will be a factor in every differential model, so the labels
must be reliable. Two sources exist: our rule-based label from the disease and
derived-from-site annotation (`general_site`, pre-processing step 02) and the
tissue labels of Shorthouse et al. (11 tissues). In addition, this notebook
shows which Shorthouse cell lines are also covered by the other data sources
relevant for later steps.

**Decision supported:** which tissue labels to use.

## Inputs

- `data/derived/cancer-cell-lines/shorthouse_v1/01_injections.rds`, `02_cell_lines.tsv`, `02_sequence_variations.tsv`
- `data/raw/cancer-cell-lines/shorthouse_github/`: tissue per injection and CCLE mutation calls of Shorthouse et al. (GitHub `shorthouse-mrc/CellLine_Metabolomics` @ cce3b15; **local only**, no licence)
- `data/raw/cancer-cell-lines/ortmayr_2019/41467_2019_9695_MOESM2_ESM.xlsx`: Ortmayr et al. 2019 cell line metadata (**local only**)
- `data/raw/cancer-cell-lines/cellosaurus.txt`: name to accession mapping

## Methods

For each Shorthouse cell line, the tissue label of Shorthouse et al. was taken
from the authors' injection table and compared with our rule-based label.
Cell line names of the other data sources were mapped to Cellosaurus
accessions by exact match after removing punctuation and case (human entries
only), preferring the primary Cellosaurus name over synonyms; names without a
unique match are reported.
Overlaps were counted on accessions.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/use_case.R"))
source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/plotting.R"))
source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/cellosaurus.R"))
config <- load_config()
derived_dir <- uc_dir(config, "derived")
raw_dir <- uc_dir(config, "raw")
fig_dir <- uc_dir(config, "output", "audit_03_tissue_and_overlaps")

injections <- readRDS(file.path(derived_dir, "01_injections.rds"))$injections
cell_lines <- readr::read_tsv(file.path(derived_dir, "02_cell_lines.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
variations <- readr::read_tsv(file.path(derived_dir, "02_sequence_variations.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
github_dir <- file.path(raw_dir, "shorthouse_github")
ortmayr_file <- file.path(raw_dir, "ortmayr_2019", "41467_2019_9695_MOESM2_ESM.xlsx")
stopifnot(dir.exists(github_dir), file.exists(ortmayr_file))
```

## 1. Our tissue labels vs the labels of Shorthouse et al.

```{r tissue-compare}
# tissue label of the paper per injection, collapsed per cell line
paper_tissue <- readr::read_csv(file.path(github_dir, "Cellline_mappings_shorthouse.csv"),
                                show_col_types = FALSE, name_repair = "unique_quiet") %>%
    transmute(injection_id = as.character(dsIdx), tissue_paper = Tissue)
tissues <- injections %>%
    left_join(paper_tissue, by = "injection_id") %>%
    group_by(line) %>%
    summarise(tissue_paper = paste(sort(unique(tissue_paper)), collapse = "; "), .groups = "drop") %>%
    left_join(select(cell_lines, line, general_site, derived_site, disease_clean), by = "line")

# the two label sets name some tissues differently
same_tissue <- c("Lung/Pleura" = "Lung", "Urinary bladder" = "Bladder")
tissues <- tissues %>%
    mutate(ours = coalesce(unname(same_tissue[general_site]), general_site),
           agree = ours == tissue_paper)
c(lines = nrow(tissues), agree = sum(tissues$agree, na.rm = TRUE))

# cross-table as heatmap
p <- count(tissues, ours = general_site, paper = tissue_paper) %>%
    ggplot(aes(paper, ours, fill = n)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white") +
    geom_text(aes(label = n), size = 3) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "#DEEBF7", high = "#08519C") +
    labs(x = "Tissue (Shorthouse et al.)", y = "Our rule-based label", fill = "Lines",
         title = "Both label sets agree for most lines") +
    theme_uc() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
save_figure(p, "tissue_ours_vs_paper", fig_dir, width = 9, height = 6)
p
```

The lines where the labels differ, with the annotation they are based on:

```{r tissue-disagree}
tissues %>%
    filter(!agree | is.na(agree)) %>%
    select(line, ours = general_site, paper = tissue_paper, derived_site, disease_clean) %>%
    preview_table(caption = "Lines with different tissue labels")
```

```{r tissue-counts}
# number of lines per tissue with the labels of the paper
p <- count(tissues, tissue_paper) %>%
    ggplot(aes(reorder(tissue_paper, n), n)) +
    geom_col(fill = "#0072B2") +
    geom_text(aes(label = n), hjust = -0.2, size = 3) +
    coord_flip() +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Cell lines", title = "Cell lines per tissue (Shorthouse et al.)",
         subtitle = sprintf("%d lines", nrow(tissues))) +
    theme_uc()
save_figure(p, "lines_per_tissue_paper", fig_dir)
p
```

After the decision, step 02 harmonises the labels (renaming plus documented
overrides in `config.yml`). The final label `tissue` should now equal the
paper's label except for NCIH460, which the paper labels inconsistently:

```{r tissue-final}
final_check <- tissues %>%
    left_join(select(cell_lines, line, tissue), by = "line") %>%
    mutate(same = tissue == tissue_paper)
c(lines = nrow(final_check), same_as_paper = sum(final_check$same, na.rm = TRUE))
final_check %>%
    filter(!same | is.na(same)) %>%
    select(line, tissue_final = tissue, tissue_paper) %>%
    preview_table(caption = "Final tissue labels differing from the paper")
```

## 2. Overlap with other data sources

```{r name-mapping}
# Cellosaurus names and synonyms, normalised (case and punctuation removed)
cellosaurus <- read_cellosaurus(file.path(raw_dir, config$cellosaurus$file))$entries %>% filter(human)
normalise <- function(x) toupper(gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]", "", x))
# the primary Cellosaurus name (priority 1) wins over synonyms (priority 2),
# because many short names (e.g. PC-3) are also synonyms of other lines
name_index <- bind_rows(
    transmute(cellosaurus, ac, name = id, priority = 1L),
    cellosaurus %>%
        transmute(ac, name = coalesce(synonyms, "")) %>%
        separate_rows(name, sep = ";\\s*") %>%
        filter(name != "") %>%
        mutate(priority = 2L)
) %>%
    transmute(ac, key = normalise(name), priority) %>%
    distinct()

# map names to accessions: best priority only, and keep only unique matches
map_names <- function(names) {
    tibble(name = unique(names)) %>%
        mutate(key = normalise(name)) %>%
        left_join(name_index, by = "key", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
        group_by(name) %>%
        filter(is.na(priority) | priority == min(priority)) %>%
        summarise(n_matches = n_distinct(ac, na.rm = TRUE),
                  ac = if (n_distinct(ac, na.rm = TRUE) == 1) first(na.omit(ac)) else NA_character_,
                  .groups = "drop")
}

# Ortmayr et al. 2019: cell line names and tissue (header in row 3 of the sheet)
ortmayr <- readxl::read_excel(ortmayr_file, sheet = "Cell_metadata", skip = 2) %>%
    select(name = `Cell line`, tissue = Tissue) %>%
    filter(!is.na(name))
ortmayr_map <- map_names(ortmayr$name)

# CCLE mutation calls used by Shorthouse et al. (names are Cellosaurus names)
ccle_calls <- readr::read_csv(file.path(github_dir, "Mutations_in_celllines.csv"),
                              show_col_types = FALSE, name_repair = "unique_quiet")
ccle_map <- map_names(unique(ccle_calls$CellLineName_Cellosaurus))

# names that could not be mapped uniquely
bind_rows(
    mutate(filter(ortmayr_map, is.na(ac)), source = "Ortmayr 2019"),
    mutate(filter(ccle_map, is.na(ac)), source = "CCLE calls (Shorthouse)")
) %>%
    select(source, name, n_matches) %>%
    preview_table(caption = "Names without a unique Cellosaurus match")
```

```{r overlap}
# sets of accessions; NCIH460DNP53 shares the parental accession and is left out
shorthouse_ac <- cell_lines$accession[!cell_lines$engineered]
sets <- tibble(accession = unique(c(shorthouse_ac, ortmayr_map$ac, ccle_map$ac))) %>%
    filter(!is.na(accession)) %>%
    mutate(
        `Shorthouse metabolomics` = accession %in% shorthouse_ac,
        `Ortmayr metabolomics` = accession %in% ortmayr_map$ac,
        `CCLE mutation calls (Shorthouse)` = accession %in% ccle_map$ac,
        `Cellosaurus variations` = accession %in% variations$accession
    )

# how many Shorthouse lines each source covers
sets %>%
    filter(`Shorthouse metabolomics`) %>%
    summarise(across(-accession, sum))

p <- ComplexUpset::upset(
    as.data.frame(sets), intersect = setdiff(names(sets), "accession"),
    name = "Data sources", width_ratio = 0.25, min_size = 1,
    base_annotations = list("Cell lines" = ComplexUpset::intersection_size(text = list(size = 3)))
) + patchwork::plot_annotation(title = "Overlap of cell lines between data sources (Cellosaurus accessions)")
save_figure(p, "overlap_upset", fig_dir, width = 10, height = 6)
p
```

```{r overlap-tissue}
# lines with metabolomics in both data sets, by tissue (Shorthouse labels)
both <- cell_lines %>%
    filter(accession %in% ortmayr_map$ac, !engineered) %>%
    left_join(select(tissues, line, tissue_paper), by = "line")
count(both, tissue_paper, sort = TRUE)
```

## Interpretation and proposed decision

- Our rule-based labels and the labels of Shorthouse et al. agree for nearly
  all lines. Where they differ, the paper's label is the more plausible one in
  most cases: our rules are misled by lines with two disease annotations (M14,
  PC3) and fall back to the sampling site for breast cancers from pleural
  effusions (MDAMB436, T47D), producing the non-tissue label "Body fluid".
- The paper labels three lines as "Unknown" (184A1, a non-malignant breast
  epithelial line; NCIH460DNP53; SR8714) and NCIH460 as "Lung; Unknown"
  (lung is correct).
- The overlap shows how many Shorthouse lines have Ortmayr metabolomics and
  CCLE mutation calls; this matters for the mutation comparison (Audit 4).

**Decision (2026-10-28):** keep the rule-based labels (derived from
Cellosaurus and EV1, so independent of the unlicensed GitHub repository),
renamed to the eleven tissues of Shorthouse et al., and set the eight lines
that differ to the authors' label, each with a documented reason in
`config.yml`. NCIH460 keeps "Lung". The three "Unknown" lines are excluded from
tissue-adjusted models.

sessionInfo()
